sentences.text: This petition has been filed challenging the Public Notice dated 31st July 2025, issued under Section 21 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act 2013 ('Act of 2013'), with respect to the land described in the prayer clause.

sentences.text:
For ease of reference, the said prayer is extracted as under:
This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.

It is stated that this acquisition forms part of Review Petition (C) No. 418 of 2023 in Civil Appeal No. 8505 of 2016 which was included in the batch of petitions, which were disposed of by the Supreme Court in Govt. of NCT of Delhi vs. K.L Rathi Steels Limited and Ors. 2024 7 SCC 315,
where directions were passed inter alia in paragraph 128 of the said judgement.

Pursuant to Supreme Court's judgement, the directions were given, and a mandatory time schedule was provided for the fresh acquistion under the Act of 2013, the impugned notices have been issued on 31st July 2025, which as per the petitioner, deviates from the scheme prescribed under the Act of 2013 and the schedule fixed by the Apex Court.
This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.

It is pointed out that previously the Court has taken a view in similar matters, inter alia in Lokesh Lochav & Anr vs. Govt. NCT of Delhi & Ors in W.P (C) 11820/2025, in which following directions were passed: "8.

sentences.text: We make it clear that no further action pursuant to the notice under Section 21 of the Act of 2013, as against the land of the petitioner, be undertaken till returnable date.

9. The aforesaid injunction order is passed taking in view the prima facie satisfaction by this Court that the schedule as ordered by the Apex Court in the matter of DDA v. Tejpal (supra) appears to be mandatory in nature."
4.
Accordingly, since the matters are similary placed, issue notice.

5. Notices are accepted by Mr. Sanjay Kumar Pathak, Standing Counsel appears for respondent nos.1 & 2, Ms. Theepa Murugesan, Senior Panel Counsel (SPC) who appears for respondent no.3/Union of India (UOI) and Ms. Malvika Kapila Kalra, Advocate who appears for respondent no.
